messages.subject: Implementing logdensity.bin (JAGS) equivalent in nimble
parts:
I am working on a wildlife resource selection study. In the past I have used JAGS for these models, but I would like to use nimble given the number and size of models I need to run.

Within my models, I use weighting that is commonly referred to as "pfix" models in the literature. The section of code that accomplishes this looks as follows:

    # Likelihood and ONES Trick for weighting
    for( j in 1:NOBS){
      y[j] ~ dbern(p[j])
      log.like[j] <- (1/PFix[j]) * logdensity.bin(y[j],p[j],1) #For computing WAIC and weighting
      ones[j] ~ dbern(exp(log.like[j]))

NOBS is the total number of observations in my data, PFix is a weight associated with every observation in the data, p[j] is the output from logistic model, and ones is a dummy vector of ones with the same length as NOBS.

When I run my model, nimble gives an error that logdensity.bin does not exist. In JAGS, all distributions have a log density function associated with them. Is there an equivalent in nimble?

Thank you for any guidance

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Implementing logdensity.bin (JAGS) equivalent in nimble
parts:
The short answer is no, and that's primarily because nimble allows you to write your own functions and distributions rather than using tricks like this for density calculations. nimble also supports WAIC. I'm not sure what the weighting scheme is here. The quickest way to make your code work in the way it is written would be to provide logdensity.bin as a user-defined function in nimble. It would look like this:

logdensity.bin <- nimbleFunction(
  function(y = double(), p = double(), size = double()) {
    return(dbin(y, prob = p, size = size, log = TRUE))
    returnType(double())
  }) 
You could hard-code the 1 instead of taking the size argument if you want.

I hope that makes sense. In case you haven't poked around our documentation, the User Manual at r-nimble.org has much more about writing your own ("user-defined") functions and distributions to use in models. As noted above I suspect there will be a cleaner way to do what you want. HTH!

Perry

messages.subject: Re: Implementing logdensity.bin (JAGS) equivalent in nimble
parts: Did you define the logdensity.bin nimbleFunction before calling nimbleModel? The error is saying that when nimbleModel tries to construct the DAG of relationships among nodes, it can't find logdensity.bin as a nimbleFunction (and the alternative would be if all inputs are constants so it can call it as an R function once and only once, which is not a very common situation). Feel free to send the code, reduced to a minimal example if possible, off-list if you prefer. -Perry
